The recorded figure is 1,531 lines cut and marked, 0 cut unmarked. In this bundle's spec-index.md, each line without a mark ends at a full stop, and the two cut lines (FR-006 at the cap, SC-001 after its sentence) end ' [...]'. Under the arbiter's ruling, where a marked cut falls, the cap and the sentence heuristic's boundary are not defects. Aside, not a finding: spec-index.md's heading names only the 420 cut as marked.

decisions.summary: Round 3 fix 2: `own_run` stops a feature number's run of ids at its last comma, or before its last id, when the text after it opens 'in N's', 'of feature N' or another possessive

decisions.summary: Residue of fix 2: ids inside the clause that stops the run (the clause the plan itself calls one naming another source, e.g. 'D1 and D3 in 999's sections') are not read as N's. They fall to the reviewed feature, with no marker and no NOT FOUND line
decisions.why: This section's own bundle shows it. blocks.md names D1 and D3 only on line 5, as 'D1 and D3 in 999's sections', yet spec-cited.md carries feature 451's own D1 (One make detector) and D3 (A background run's end) with no marker. T46's line, and checklist item 1, say an id named with another feature's number is 'never' carried from the reviewed feature. The plan's own own_run wording treats 'in N's' as naming another source, so it cannot also read those ids as bare. This is the T42 failure the task exists to end: the wrong feature's text, unmarked. It is a known defect left, and Found-and-left does not list it. It is not of the kind the arbiter excluded, which concerned where a marked index cut falls. Fix: read ids in a clause naming feature N as N's (looked up there, or NOT FOUND), with N's own name read as this feature's; or at the least carry them marked, as the bare form is. How often this occurs in real plans is not measured in this bundle.

blocks: ### T48 (the bundle read ids inside a clause naming another feature by its number as the reviewed feature's, filed by the round arbiter on `ask:451-T46-fourth-round` (accept, 2026-11-20) to be measured first; measured 2026-11-21: 4 of the 5 real such clauses across every plan handed the reviewer the reviewed feature's same-named id, unmarked, method below)
### T48 Approach (checklist part A)

decisions.summary: Fix the clause reading rather than only file it: measured first over 327 plan.md and plan-done.md files, 5 real clauses naming another feature, 4 of them handing the reviewer the reviewed feature's same-named text unmarked; named() now reads such ids as N's, carried from N or named NOT FOUND, red test first.
decisions.why: The arbiter's ruling on ask:451-T46-fourth-round says: file the residue, measure first how often such a clause names another feature across specs/*/plan.md and plan-done.md, and fix it only if a real one hands a reviewer the wrong text. The plan measured first, found 4 real wrong-text cases, and fixed the reading as the ruling describes.

decisions.summary: The clause forms read: 'in N's', 'of feature N', and 'from N'.
decisions.why: The ruling's two forms are examples of 'a clause naming feature N'. 'from N' names a feature by its number in the same way. The plan measured that none of the 8 clauses reads a count as a feature number.

decisions.summary: QUALIFIED gets a third branch: a run of ids that no number names, followed by such a clause, belongs entirely to the clause's feature. ANOTHER captures the clause's number, so the part of a numbered run cut off at such a clause belongs to that feature.
decisions.why: This is how the ruling's residue ('<ids> in N's') gets read as N's. The plan measured every such run among the 8 as holding one id, and a misread costs a line marked with the clause's feature or a NOT FOUND line, never this feature's text unmarked.

decisions.summary: A clause naming the reviewed feature reads as before. A clause naming a source by another name ('in house style's') leaves its ids bare.
decisions.why: The ruling covers clauses naming a feature by number. For the reviewed feature's own number, the ruling says reading as N's carries the same text, and the plan reports that as unchanged. The other-name branch was measured: 2 real cases, both naming the feature's own work, so no wrong outcome. That is a difference, not a defect.

decisions.summary: Requirement-reader gap left and filed as T82 (lands before T22): a bold FR or SC id written without a list dash is not read, so a NOT FOUND line appears where the text exists (449's T050 against 239). It affects 24 specs, features 129 to 271.
decisions.why: This is a wrong outcome, but in a different reader (requirements) from the clause reading the ruling asked to be fixed, and it predates T48. A citation by number alone gets the same line. The ruling's row does not reach it, so leaving it does not narrow what was asked. The deferral says why it is not fixed here, names T82, and gives its order, as FR-009 requires. The case that exposed it is in plan-done.md, which no review reads.

decisions.summary: 443's plan.md line 25, which cites an id its named feature (435) does not hold, is left as written and is now named NOT FOUND.
decisions.why: A correct NOT FOUND line is not a wrong outcome, and 443's plan is outside the brief.

decisions.summary: Closing checks were measured in a detached worktree of HEAD with only T48's three files, because the clone was red from another builder's half-edited T79 file. Static, quick, and the plan crate's lint, format and cover were green. hooks-test's residual 2 suites were each green alone.
decisions.why: This is the plan's own exit procedure, not a narrowing of the GM's request or the spec. The request and the ruling set no exit for T48, and the landing's gate still decides.
